purpose: Routing index for the geometry-of-rhythm literature that pop/lib rhythm tooling is derived from.
posture: Index and citation only. Books and paywalled articles are never mirrored into the repo. Open-access PDFs are fetched into sources/ (gitignored) by fetch-sources.mjs.

checked_key.true: citation details confirmed against a primary or publisher source during a platter pass
checked_key.false: written from working knowledge; wants a verification pass before it is cited in a paper

shelves.toussaint: Toussaint's own corpus — the spine of the platter.
shelves.evenness: Maximal evenness, balance, well-formedness: what 'even' means formally.
shelves.oddity-depth: Rhythmic oddity, deepness, interval content, homometry.
shelves.distance: Rhythmic similarity and distance geometry — the morphing levers.
shelves.perception: Meter, entrainment, groove, microtiming — where the grid model stops.
shelves.spatial: Spatial hearing. Secondary shelf: the bracelet track's own thesis rests on it, so it is indexed here rather than assumed.
shelves.solkattu: Spoken rhythm: South Indian rhythmic solfège (solkattu/konnakol) as a named, oral rhythm representation.
shelves.timbre: Timbre as geometry. Secondary shelf: the same dissimilarity-to-space move applied to tone quality, indexed here because it is the platter's method applied off-rhythm.

sources.title: The Euclidean Algorithm Generates Traditional Musical Rhythms
sources.venue: Proceedings of BRIDGES: Mathematical Connections in Art, Music, and Science, Banff, Alberta, July 31 – August 3, 2005
sources.why: The catalogue. §4 lists 40+ E(k,n) rhythms with culture attributions; timelines.json is extracted from it.

sources.title: The Geometry of Musical Rhythm: What Makes a "Good" Rhythm Good?
sources.why: The synthesis. Cited by chapter throughout the digest. Never reproduced — no scans, no excerpts, no text in the repo.

sources.title: A Mathematical Analysis of African, Brazilian, and Cuban Clave Rhythms
sources.venue: BRIDGES: Mathematical Connections in Art, Music and Science, Towson University, July 27–29, 2002
sources.why: Source for the six distinguished 5-onset/16-pulse timelines (son, rumba, bossa, shiko, soukous, gahu).

sources.title: Classification and Phylogenetic Analysis of African Ternary Rhythm Timelines
sources.why: The 12-pulse ternary family and the phylogenetic-tree method applied to timelines.

sources.title: A Comparison of Rhythmic Similarity Measures
sources.venue: ISMIR 2004, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona, October 10–14
sources.why: Head-to-head of Hamming, swap, chronotonic, and interval-vector distances — decides which measure pop/lib should default to.

sources.title: Mathematical Features for Recognizing Preference in Sub-Saharan African Traditional Rhythm Timelines
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Advances in Pattern Recognition, University of Bath, August 22–25, 2005
sources.why: The actual source of the off-beatness measure. pop/minitek currently attributes off-beatness to Toussaint 2005 generically; this is the paper.

sources.title: The Geometry of Musical Rhythm
sources.venue: Japan Conference on Discrete and Computational Geometry, LNCS 3742, Springer-Verlag
sources.why: The compact statement of the geometric programme that became the book.

sources.title: Interlocking Rhythms, Duration Interval Content, Cyclotomic Sets, and the Hexachordal Theorem
sources.venue: Fourth International Workshop on Computational Music Theory, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid
sources.why: Complementary rhythms and the hexachordal theorem — the theory behind interlocking two necklaces, which the bracelet track needs.

sources.title: Computational Geometric Aspects of Rhythm, Melody, and Voice-Leading
sources.why: Survey tying the rhythm work to pitch/voice-leading geometry — the bridge if a melodic-necklace lane ever opens.

sources.title: The Distance Geometry of Music
sources.why: Proves Euclidean rhythms maximise the sum of pairwise Euclidean chord distances. This is the theorem that makes chord-sum the correct evenness measure and arc-sum the wrong one.

sources.title: Structural Properties of Euclidean Rhythms
sources.why: Main-pattern-plus-tail decomposition of E(k,n) and its Bézout connection. Gives a closed form that a generator can exploit instead of iterating Bjorklund.

sources.title: The Theory of Rep-Rate Pattern Generation in the SNS Timing System
sources.why: The algorithm itself, invented for neutron-spallation timing electronics, not music. Already implemented in pop/minitek/c/hypnotek.c.

sources.title: Maximally Even Sets
sources.why: Formalises maximal evenness for pitch-class sets; the rhythmic case is the dual. Source of the two-gap property.

sources.title: African Polyphony and Polyrhythm: Musical Structure and Methodology
sources.why: Origin of the rhythmic oddity property. Already used as a measured axis in pop/minitek/c/dubtek.c.

sources.title: Exploring the Space of Perfectly Balanced Rhythms and Scales
sources.why: Perfect balance (centre of mass at the origin) is a DIFFERENT property from maximal evenness. Distinguishing them matters: balance is the one that maps directly onto physical space.

sources.title: XronoMorph: Algorithmic Generation of Perfectly Balanced and Well-Formed Rhythms
sources.why: Closest prior art to what pop/lib will be: a working instrument built on balance + well-formedness, with a circular UI. Read before designing the API.

sources.title: Music Through Fourier Space: Discrete Fourier Transform in Music Theory
sources.why: DFT view: evenness and balance both fall out of specific Fourier coefficients of the onset indicator. The cheapest correct implementation of several measures.

sources.title: Perception of Temporal Patterns
sources.why: The C-score clock-induction model of rhythmic complexity.

sources.title: The Rhythmic Interpretation of Monophonic Music
sources.why: The LHL syncopation measure — the most-used metric-hierarchy syncopation score.

sources.title: From Polychords to Pólya: Adventures in Musical Combinatorics
sources.why: Keith's syncopation measure, and the Pólya-counting machinery for enumerating necklaces and bracelets.

sources.title: Hearing in Time: Psychological Aspects of Musical Meter
sources.why: Entrainment limits and the tempo window inside which a listener will re-parse a meter. Bounds how fast a necklace can precess and still be heard as the same necklace.

sources.title: Unlocking the Groove: Rhythm, Meter, and Musical Design in Electronic Dance Music
sources.why: Metric ambiguity and turning-the-beat-around in EDM specifically — the genre the pop lanes actually operate in.

sources.title: Embodied Mind, Situated Cognition, and Expressive Microtiming in African-American Music
sources.why: The corrective to the whole programme: the grid discards microtiming, and microtiming is where the groove lives.

sources.title: Musical Rhythm in the Age of Digital Reproduction
sources.why: Beat bins and the width of a 'moment' — why quantised necklaces feel different from played ones.

sources.title: Cognitive Isomorphisms Between Pitch and Rhythm in World Musics
sources.why: The pitch/rhythm duality that lets scale theory (deepness, ME) be imported wholesale into rhythm.

sources.title: Turning the Analysis Around: Africa-Derived Rhythms and Europe-Derived Music Theory
sources.why: Names the risk the whole platter runs: applying European-derived formalism to African-derived practice and mistaking the model for the music.
feeds: ethics section of any paper carved from this platter

sources.title: Asymmetric Rhythms and Tiling Canons
sources.why: Counts rhythmic-oddity ('asymmetric') necklaces and connects them to tiling canons.

sources.title: Rhythm and Transforms
sources.why: Signal-side counterpart: recovering periodicity from audio rather than assuming a grid.

sources.title: Spatial Hearing: The Psychophysics of Human Sound Localization
sources.why: The reference for azimuth localisation, the cone of confusion, and elevation cues. The bracelet track's thesis stands or falls on these limits.

sources.title: On the Minimum Audible Angle
sources.venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
sources.why: About 1° frontally, degrading to 10°+ at the sides. This sets the maximum n whose steps are spatially resolvable — the hard ceiling on the mapping law.

sources.title: The Precedence Effect in Sound Localization
sources.why: Onsets under ~1–5 ms fuse and the first arrival wins the position. Two necklace beads closer than that in time will not be heard as two places.

sources.title: Indian Rhythms with Dr. Levin
sources.venue: YouTube (Ben Levin Guitar Lessons), uploaded 2011-10-29, 478 s, shot/edited by Rob Berry
sources.fetch: yt-dlp into sources/ (gitignored); on-screen overlays OCR'd via macOS Vision to sources/levin-2011-indian-rhythms.ocr.txt, auto-captions cleaned to .captions.txt
sources.why: The solkattu syllable ladder (1–8), the Tom phrase-end marker, both usage modes (pulse-fixed additive meters incl. 15/16 = 3+5+7 and 17/16 = 5+5+7; beat-fixed tuplet ladder), and the 5+3+3+5 palindromic 4/4. Digest 09 is extracted from its overlays.
sources.caveat: Pedagogical demonstration by a guitarist, not a Carnatic primary source; syllable spellings vary across traditions.

sources.title: Timbre Space as a Musical Control Structure
sources.note: Also circulated as IRCAM Rapport 12/78. Bibliographic details confirmed against the scan itself; JSTOR stable URL not machine-verifiable (bot challenge). Local copy hand-placed in sources/ from the JSTOR scan shared by Sage Jenson, 2026-08-15 — not fetched by fetch-sources.mjs, since no open-access URL currently resolves.
sources.why: The canonical subjective-dissimilarity → geometry → control-lever paper: MDS timbre space (brightness × attack-bite), parallelogram timbral analogies, stream segregation as the perceptual acceptance test, breakpoint-envelope data reduction.
